name: veterinary_clinic_system_084_imaging_metadata_gap_fill
instruction: Repair file metadata in the files collection. For every row, enforce two conventions. (1) Path: the path must start with '<patient_id>/' where patient_id is the row's patient_id. If not, prepend '<patient_id>/'. (2) doc_type: for bucket 'vet-imaging', the file extension dictates doc_type: '.png' files must have doc_type 'radiograph' and '.jpg' files must have doc_type 'clinical photo'; for bucket 'vet-documents', the second path segment (the directory between patient_id and filename) is the canonical doc_type. If doc_type is wrong, update it. For each repaired row, set path_fixed='<batch_code>' and metadata_repaired='<batch_code>', and append an audit_log entry: actor='system', actor_role='system', action='FILE_METADATA_REPAIR', target_collection='files', target_id=<file_id>, details='path: <old_path> -> <new_path>; doc_type: <old_doc_type> -> <new_doc_type>', occurred_at=<episode timestamp>. Compliant rows must stay byte-identical (no extra fields). Finally, push one ops_reports row: report='file_metadata_repair', batch_code, repaired_count, repaired_ids (sorted CSV of file ids).
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session; placeholder for hardmode v2
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session; placeholder for hardmode v2

success_criteria.summary: Only non-compliant files are modified. Paths and doc_types conform to the convention. Repaired rows have path_fixed and metadata_repaired set to batch_code. One audit_log entry per repaired file with the exact action/details. One ops_reports summary with repaired_count and sorted repaired_ids. All other collections outside the blast radius are byte-identical.

checks.expect: only non-compliant files changed: missing patient_id prefix prepended and doc_type set per convention
one audit_log entry per repaired file and one ops_reports summary with repaired_count/ids
the set of repaired files is also identified via SQL and agrees with the API-derived set

hazards: Only files id 2 (patient_id '4', path '2026-05-02/hip-ventrodorsal.png', filename 'hip-ventrodorsal.png') is missing the '<patient_id>/' prefix and must be repaired to '4/2026-05-02/hip-ventrodorsal.png'. All other files already start with their patient_id and must remain byte-identical except for the added tag fields.

For vet-imaging bucket the doc_type must be derived from filename extension: '.png' files -> 'radiograph' (ids 1, 2) and '.jpg' files -> 'clinical photo' (ids 3, 7). Setting every imaging file to a single doc_type would break half the rows.

For vet-documents bucket the doc_type must equal the second path segment: id 4 'rabies-certificate', id 5 'boarding-consent', id 6 'anesthesia-consent', id 8 'referral-letter'. Altering these to match filename substrings would be wrong.
Compliant rows must not receive path_fixed or metadata_repaired (only repaired rows get the tags). An agent that tags every row fails the canary that expects unchanged rows to be byte-identical.
The audit_log entries must have exact actor/role/action/target_collection and a details string showing the old and new path/doc_type. Missing or generic audit entries fail.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Combines path repair, doc_type normalization by bucket-specific rules, audit logging, and a repair summary. The decoy is a single missing-prefix file amid otherwise compliant imaging and document rows; the doc_type rules differ by bucket, forcing the agent to inspect both filename and path segment.
